name: Grand Hyatt Goa
positioning: Bayfront resort on 28 acres of tropical gardens overlooking Bambolim Bay in Goa
best_for: Travelers wanting a garden resort with bay views and balconies in every room
Families looking for a kids' pool and an on-site adventure park
Spa-focused stays built around Shamana Spa

facts.text: Grand Hyatt Goa overlooks the waters of Bambolim Bay.
The resort spreads across 28 acres of tropical gardens and lawns that roll down to the water's edge.
The architecture features soaring doors and windows, tiled roofs and recessed balconies with reflecting pools, alongside a ruined chapel and ancient banyans.
Every room has a balcony with views of sunsets, the free-form swimming pool or tropical gardens.
Suites have a whirlpool on the balcony overlooking gardens and ocean.
Rooms have a marble bathroom with a tub and a separate walk-in rain shower.
The Presidential Suite has an outdoor tub overlooking Bambolim Bay, a private kitchen and a personal butler.
Shamana Spa blends modern therapies with ancient Indian traditions.
The outdoor pool area has a leisure pool and a kids' pool facing Bambolim Bay.
There is also an indoor lap pool, with separate steam and sauna facilities next to the whirlpools.
The Dining Room is an all-day restaurant with five live kitchens, including Asian, Indian and Italian choices.
Pool Bar and Grill sits steps from the bay, by the free-form outdoor pool.

highlights.text: The resort spreads across 28 acres of tropical gardens and lawns that roll down to the edge of Bambolim Bay.
The architecture features soaring doors and windows, tiled roofs and reflecting pools, alongside a ruined chapel and ancient banyans.
Suites have a whirlpool on the balcony overlooking gardens and ocean.
The outdoor pool area has a leisure pool and a kids' pool facing Bambolim Bay.
An adventure park offers a zip line, sky cycle, wall climbing and a rope course.

considerations.text: Grand Club lounge access, with breakfast, all-day coffee and tea and evening drinks and canapes, comes with Club Access rooms.
WhataHotel notes the large resort may feel less intimate.
